programme.desc: Liz McIvor tells the story of the people who operated the canal boats, carrying fuel and goods around the country.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: The flood of funds into sculptural projects during the burgeoning British Empire unleashed a new, yet remarkably unorthodox, golden age. The greatest sculptors of the 18th and 19th centuries were mavericks who bucked prevailing trends - geniuses like John Flaxman, Francis Chantrey and Alfred Gilbert. Sooke reveals the technical breakthroughs behind their key works.

programme.title: British History's Biggest Fibs with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: Lucy debunks the `Glorious Revolution'. In 1688, the British Isles were invaded by a huge army led by Dutch prince, William of Orange. With his English wife Mary he stole the throne from Mary's father, the Catholic King James II. This was the death knell for absolute royal power and laid the foundations of our constitutional monarchy.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: This is the story of the men who built the canals, the navigators or `navvies'. They represented an `army' of hard physical men who were capable of enduring tough labour for long hours. Many roved the countryside looking for work and a better deal. They gained a reputation as troublesome outsiders, fond of drinking and living a life of ungodly debauchery. But who were they?

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Shire horses, lifeboat heroes and a rugby team who train on the beach are among friends old and new that Gareth and Maureen Edwards meet on a trip away to St Davids, Pembrokeshire.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Plants
programme.desc: It has long been known that plants can move, but recent studies have found that they can also smell, touch and taste, and have other surprising senses, allowing people to look at them with fresh eyes.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: A seasonal tale of how the Garden of Eden really was invaded not by a bad snake, but by one of the nation's favourite little birds.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: Bruce Parry treks into the high mountains in the tiny Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan, to live with the isolated Layap people. They are devout Buddhists and yak herders, cut off from the outside world for half the year by deep snow.

programme.title: Lowry: A Simple Man
programme.desc: A ballet celebrating the centenary of the birth of painter LS Lowry, first broadcast in 1987. Starring Christopher Gable and Moira Shearer. Carl Davis conducts the BBC Philharmonic. Introduced by actor Albert Finney.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis explores how, by the Wars of the Roses, castles were under attack from a new threat, the cannon, but survived into the Tudor era only to find their whole purpose challenged.

programme.title: Beautiful Equations
programme.desc: Art critic Matt Collings plunges into the world of mathematical equations. As he explores the most famous equations in science, Einstein's E equals mc2, Dirac's equation on anti-matter and Newton's laws of gravity, Matt realises that concepts of beauty and elegance have been used by many scientists to advance their work.

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Maureen has arranged a trip the spectacular Brecon Beacons. But it's not the usual walks amid epic mountain scenery on the agenda. In a first for both, the childhood sweethearts enlist in tank school. After donning cam cream and military gear, the couple get a lesson in controlling a full-sized tank.

programme.title: The Bridge: Fifty Years Across The Forth
programme.desc: A unique amateur film provides the centrepiece of a documentary celebrating the 50th anniversary of one of Scotland's great landmarks, the Forth Road Bridge.

programme.title: The Read
programme.sub-title: The 39 Steps: The Read with John Hannah
programme.desc: BAFTA-nominated actor John Hannah gives a thrilling reading performance of this classic text. Murder, conspiracy and espionage are the themes of John Buchan's gripping novel, set against the backdrop of WWI, that sees Richard Hannay, a bored adventurer, become embroiled in a plot to assassinate a political figure.

programme.title: The 39 Steps
programme.desc: Richard Hannay, pursued by the police for a murder he did not commit, and by an international spy-ring for information he does not possess, finds himself fleeing across the desolate Scottish moors, handcuffed to a beautiful blonde.

programme.title: Calendar Girls
programme.desc: Based on the true story of 12 ladies from Yorkshire baring all for charity. When one of the women's husbands dies from leukaemia, they decide that their prim and proper fundraising efforts need a bit of a shake-up. They find a more compelling way to raise money - by starring in a nude calendar. Their modest hopes of selling a few hundred copies around the village are outstripped when it becomes a worldwide sensation.

programme.title: The Horizon Guide to AI
programme.desc: The BBC's Horizon programme began in 1964, and since then has produced films looking at computer technology and the emergence of `artificial intelligence'. The dreams always begin with ideology and optimism, only for this optimism to be replaced with suspicion that AI machines will take over. However, as the archive shows, throughout each decade once people have learnt to live with the new emerging technology of the time, the pattern begins again.

programme.title: St David's Day at the BBC
programme.desc: To celebrate St David's Day, this trip through the BBC's music archives features a selection of tracks from some of the most important and innovative Welsh artists of the past few decades. programme.title: Dame Shirley Bassey: Electric Proms
programme.desc: Trevor Nelson and Edith Bowman present highlights of Dame Shirley Bassey's special performance for the `Electric Proms' from London's Roundhouse. The British icon performs a set packed with classic tracks like `Big Spender' and `Goldfinger' and premieres new songs from her forthcoming album, `The Performance', produced by Bond composer David Arnold.
